Methodological Rigor & Homonym Conflation Prevention

In Arab patronymic nomenclature, given names such as Mohamed, Ali, and Ahmed represent over 35% of all male names in Tunisia. Conflating different families because their fathers share a common ancestor named "Mohamed" creates spurious mega-lineages.

This nationwide network adheres strictly to empirical co-presence and deterministic pedigree verification:

  • No Grandparent Conflation: Voters are never joined on first names alone across different households or centers.
  • Nuclear Sibling Cliques: Formed only when voters share the exact identical (Father Name, Grandfather Name, Surname) AND register at the exact same neighborhood polling center.
  • Direct Parental Links: Formed only when a father is explicitly registered in the same center with matching generation rank and CIN generation chronology.
  • Privacy Safeguards: All CIN numbers are masked to the last 3 digits, ensuring 0% identity leakage while allowing exact genealogical disambiguation.
